title: Choosing a Paradigm and Combining Approaches
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its role in program design.
Trace example behavior and state changes.
Apply it to a simple scenario.

understand.concept: Paradigm selection should fit the requirements, constraints, language, team, testability, and likely future change. Programs can combine procedural, object-oriented, functional, declarative, and event-driven approaches. A clear, maintainable solution matters more than applying one style everywhere.
understand.whyItMatters: Paradigm choices affect clarity, complexity, testability, and change cost. Comparing alternatives encourages simpler, suitable designs.
understand.analogy: Selecting a tool for a task involves considering requirements and constraints; programming choices also depend on language, team, and runtime.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies software behavior and design trade-offs.

explain.narrative: Identify the event or requirement, the code that responds, and the state or output that changes. Consider timing, asynchronous behavior, error handling, and responsiveness. When choosing a design, compare alternatives against concrete requirements and testability.
